newsitem.title: GERMANY: German chemical industry agrees opt-out clause.
newsitem.headline: German chemical industry agrees opt-out clause.

text.p: West German chemical industry employers and unions have agreed to an opt-out clause in their wage contract enabling companies hard hit by the slow economy to pay lower wages to their workers.

Chemical workers union IG Chemie and employer representatives said that investment in German plants could be a justification for paying lower wages. The BAVC association of chemical industry employers, meanwhile, agreed to ensure employment levels.
The west German chemical industry represents around 590,000 workers and around 1,700 firms.
The German chemical industry is generally regarded among the most flexible of German industries on wage contracts, reaching agreements.
